sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Knox County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Knox County splits the work among several offices, and a seller will usually deal with three of them. The County Treasurer, in the courthouse in Galesburg, bills and collects the tax. The county Assessment Office, reachable at 309-345-3845, handles exemptions and the Board of Review appeal forms. Township assessors set the values, and the County Clerk handles tax sale certificates and redemption.

Knox County has three assessing districts. A North District assessor covers Rio, Ontario, Walnut Grove, Lynn, Henderson, Sparta, Copley, Victoria, Persifer and Truro townships. A South District assessor covers Galesburg, Knox, Cedar, Orange, Haw Creek, Elba, Indian Point, Chestnut, Maquon and Salem townships. The City of Galesburg has its own township assessor. Which one answers your question depends on where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Knox County itself?
sections.html:
Knox County covers 716 square miles of land in west central Illinois, with Galesburg as county seat and largest city. It was organized in 1825 from Fulton County. Neighbors are Mercer, Henry, Stark, Peoria, Fulton and Warren Counties, and ten school districts serve it, among them Galesburg CUSD 205, Knoxville CUSD 202 and ROWVA CUSD 208.

The county is shrinking slowly. The 2020 Census counted 49,967 residents and the July 2025 estimate is 47,767, a drop of 4.4% from the 2020 base. Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median home value of $111,900, an owner-occupied rate of 70.8% and a median household income of $57,030. The bureau recorded one building permit in the county for 2025, and 23.9% of residents are 65 or older.

Low values change the tax picture. A bill that looks modest in dollars can still be a large share of a house's worth, so a stale assessment is worth checking before listing.

sections.h2: When are Knox County property taxes due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
The 2025 tax year bills, collected in 2026, were due in two installments: July 1 and September 1, 2026. Both dates have passed. Knox County mails one bill a year with a detachable stub for each installment, so check the dates printed on the current bill or ask the Treasurer.

Knox County late penalty on 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (source: Knox County Treasurer, Important Dates)
DateFirst installmentSecond installment
July 2, 20261.50%Not yet due
August 2, 20263.00%Not yet due
September 2, 20264.50%1.50%
October 2, 20266.00%3.00%
November 2, 20267.50%4.50%

The Treasurer explains that the penalty is 1.5% a month, is not prorated and takes effect the day after each due date. A bill that never arrived does not cancel the tax, citing 35 ILCS 200/20-15.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Knox County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Treasurer lists several routes, and the payment stub must go with any check:

  • Mail or bring a check to the Treasurer's Office, payable to Knox County Collector; the cancelled check is your receipt
  • Use a courthouse drop box, one at the curb on the north side on Tompkins Street and one at the exit of the parking lot, checks only and no envelopes provided
  • Pay at a Knox County bank, except Wells Fargo, which asked not to take them
  • Pay by credit or debit card for a fee of 2.35% or $2.95, whichever is higher

A postmark is accepted before the tax sale. Drop box payments collected at 8:30 a.m. are posted as the prior day's business. If a mortgage escrow account pays your tax, the Treasurer reminds owners that monitoring the bank's payments is their own responsibility.

sections.h2: How does Knox County set the assessed value of a home?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1, at a required 33.33% level of fair cash value, using sales from the prior three years. For 2026 the county used 2023 through 2025 sales. State equalization factors are then applied: the 2026 factor was 1.0724 for Galesburg Township and 1.0758 for the City of Galesburg, 1.0132 for Rio, Walnut Grove, Henderson and Persifer, and 1.0125 for Ontario, Sparta and Copley.

Lynn, Truro, Victoria, Elba and Salem townships were on the quadrennial general assessment cycle in 2026. The county's own formula for a bill is simple: final equalized assessed value, minus exemptions, times the tax rate. To test your number, divide the assessment by 33.33% and compare the result to what the house would really sell for.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Knox County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with your township assessor, then file a written appeal with the Board of Review. The appeal is about value, not about the amount of the tax. For the 2026 assessment year the window ran from September 17 to October 19, 2026, with a 4 p.m. deadline on the last day, so it has closed. Windows move each year, and the county accepts only that year's forms.

  • Attach evidence, such as a recent independent appraisal or sales of similar homes
  • The Board sends a notice with an informal ruling
  • If you disagree, you have ten days from the notice date to accept a formal hearing
  • After a final decision, you have thirty days to appeal to the Property Tax Appeal Board

The Knox Board of Review meets only when needed. Call the Assessment Office at 309-345-3845 for the current year's forms and dates.

sections.h2: Which Knox County exemptions can lower the bill?
sections.html:
The county posts the homeowner exemptions and applications on its assessment pages. Its Treasurer's page describes the main ones:

  • Owner occupied: up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value
  • Senior homestead, age 65 or older: $5,000 off
  • Senior assessment freeze: frozen taxable value for those 65 or older, with household income of $65,000 or less on the Treasurer's page, and the Assessment Office lists $75,000 for 2026
  • Home improvement: up to $25,000 of assessed value for four years

Returning veterans, disabled persons and disabled veterans have their own exemptions. The county asks for applications by September 30 each year but accepts them through December 31. A buyer who will live in the house should call the assessment office after January 1 of the year following the sale to confirm the homestead exemption is on the parcel.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Knox County taxes at the tax sale?
sections.html:
Knox County holds an annual tax sale, normally in mid-November, and all delinquent taxes are sold then. The county publishes the list of delinquent taxes in local newspapers in mid-October. Under Public Act 104-0553, Knox County elected to acquire all delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026. The trustee then holds an auction each year for parcels it has gone for deed on.

The County Clerk's Office handles tax sale certificates and can be reached at 309-345-6753. The Treasurer cannot give legal advice on delinquent taxes. Anyone selling a house with unpaid tax should ask the Treasurer for the payoff and have it cleared at closing, before the parcel reaches the sale.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Knox County, Illinois?
faqs.a: For the 2025 tax year, collected in 2026, the installments were due July 1 and September 1, 2026. Check the dates printed on your current bill, since the Treasurer mails one bill with a stub for each installment.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty on Knox County property tax?
faqs.a: The penalty is 1.5% per month on the unpaid balance, and it is not prorated. It starts the day after each due date.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Knox County assessment?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Review accepted 2026 appeals from September 17 to October 19, 2026, and the law bars it from taking complaints after the deadline. Ask the Assessment Office at 309-345-3845 about next year's window.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Knox County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Treasurer's Office in the Knox County courthouse in Galesburg, by mail, in a courthouse drop box, at most local banks, or by card for a fee. Checks go to the Knox County Collector.

faqs.q: When does Knox County hold its tax sale?
faqs.a: The Treasurer says the annual sale is normally held in mid-November, after a list of delinquent taxes is published in mid-October. The County Clerk handles the sale certificates.
